payload.title: What Are the Nigerian Wedding Traditions You Did Not Know?
payload.excerpt: Nigerian wedding traditions family by family, from the Yoruba introduction and engagement to the Hausa-Fulani nikah and kamu and Igbo igba nkwu, then aso ebi, spraying and the white wedding, with notes for Nigerian-Australian couples.
key_takeaways: Yoruba, Igbo and Hausa-Fulani weddings follow different customs, and many couples pair a traditional wedding with a church wedding or nikah on another day.
In many Igbo families, the bride carries a cup of palm wine through the guests at the public ceremony to find her groom.
At many Nigerian receptions, guests dance up to the couple and spray notes on them, and parents and close family take their turn on the floor.
As at November 2026, Smartraveller advises Australians to "Reconsider your need to travel" to Nigeria, and these customs travel well to a wedding in Australia or at another destination.

faq.q: Why do Nigerians spray money at weddings?
faq.a: At many Nigerian receptions, spraying is part of the dancing. Guests dance up to the couple and place notes on them while the band plays. Parents and close family take their turn, and friends of the couple often gather the notes from the floor as the dancing goes on.

faq.q: Do Nigerian couples have two weddings?
faq.a: Many do: a traditional wedding led by the families, and a church wedding or nikah on a separate day.

faq.q: What is the difference between bride price and dowry in a Nigerian wedding?
faq.a: Families usually speak of the bride price: what the groom and his family present to the bride's family, alongside the items on the family's list. Many people use "dowry" loosely for the same exchange. In Ezinifite-Aguata, an Igbo community in Anambra State, the father-in-law takes part of the bride price and returns the rest, saying he is not selling his daughter.

faq.q: Who pays for a traditional Nigerian wedding?
faq.a: It depends on the family. In many families, the groom and his family bring the bride price and the list, and the costs of the celebration are shared in many different ways. Agree the arrangement between both families early, starting with a few questions: which ceremonies each family will host, who covers the venue and catering for each day, what the bride's family will provide alongside the list, and who will speak for each side when the list is settled.

faq.q: What is aso ebi and who wears it?
faq.a: Aso ebi is the fabric chosen for a wedding and worn by family and close friends, so each side of the room is dressed in matching colour. Guests usually buy the fabric and arrange their own tailoring.

faq.q: What do men wear to a Nigerian wedding?
faq.a: At many Yoruba weddings, men wear a flowing agbada or a tunic and trousers with a fila cap, often in aṣọ-òkè, which is worn by both men and women. Men in aso ebi wear the family's chosen fabric.

faq.q: How long does a Nigerian traditional wedding last?
faq.a: The public ceremony usually fills an afternoon and runs into the evening. In many Igbo families the stages before it, from the first visit to the bride price, take place over several visits.
